LAB_05 visual walkthrough
Cyber Defense 420-D03-AB, NorthMaple Accounting Inc. (fictional)

LAB_05, step by step: Network Device Security and Network Firewall

Each step of the lab has a short animation that shows what you click and type, followed by the three things to remember. The step numbers are the same as in the lab document LAB05_Network_Device_Security_and_Network_Firewall.md, which remains the complete procedure.

The animations loop. Use Pause and Restart under each one, or Pause all at the top. A small red number next to a title is a footnote: it tells you what may look different on a newer version.

Part 1: build and lock the firewall

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

1Snapshot every VM2

  • In VirtualBox, select each VM (Virtual Machine), open Snapshots and click Take.
  • Name the snapshot before-LAB05.
  • Any later mistake can now be undone in seconds.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

2Create the lab "Internet" network3

  • Run one VBoxManage natnetwork add command for nm-wan (10.0.2.0/24, with DHCP, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol).
  • Check it with VBoxManage natnetwork list.
  • The internal networks nm-lan, nm-dmz and nm-srv need no command: they appear when you type their names.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

3Download and verify OPNsense 26.745

  • Architecture amd64, image type dvd, the nearest mirror.
  • Compute the SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit) fingerprint and compare it with the checksum file.
  • Decompress the .bz2 file to get the ISO (disc image) file.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

4Create the VM NM-FW012

  • New VM: BSD, FreeBSD (64-bit), tick Skip Unattended Installation; 2048 MB, 2 CPUs (Central Processing Units), 20 GB.
  • Four adapters in this order: 1 nm-lan, 2 nm-wan, 3 nm-dmz, 4 nm-srv.
  • OPNsense makes the first card LAN (Local Area Network) and the second WAN (Wide Area Network).

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

5Install OPNsense6

  • Log in as installer / opnsense.
  • Install (UFS, Unix File System) on ada0, Last Chance: Yes, swap: Yes.
  • Set a new root password, Complete Install, remove the disc.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

6Console: interfaces and LAN address7

  • Menu 1: WAN em1, LAN em0, OPT1 em2, OPT2 em3.
  • Menu 2: LAN 192.168.10.1/24, no DHCP server, keep HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure).
  • Write down the WAN address: it is your FW-WAN-IP for Step 18.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

7First web login and the wizard8

  • From NM-LWS01, open https://192.168.10.1 and accept the lab-only certificate warning.
  • Wizard: hostname nm-fw01, domain northmaple.lab, WAN DHCP.
  • Untick Block RFC1918 Private Networks, a lab-only change: write it down. Keep bogon blocking.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

8Update to 26.7.4 or newer9

  • System ▸ Firmware ▸ Status: Check for updates, Update, reboot.
  • The dashboard must show 26.7.4 or newer.
  • Snapshot NM-FW01 as fw-installed.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

9Enable and name DMZ and SERVERS10

  • Interfaces ▸ Assignments: OPT1 = DMZ (Demilitarized Zone), OPT2 = SERVERS.
  • Enable each one with Static IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4): 192.168.20.1/24 and 192.168.30.1/24.
  • Save, then Apply.

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

10Secure the management access11

  • Create the named administrator nmadmin (group admins).
  • HTTPS on port 443 and SSH (Secure Shell) listening on LAN only, no root login, console password.
  • Prove that root / opnsense fails, and keep an encrypted backup (do not submit it).

Part 1, Class 11 (today)

11Start the device registry12

  • Open L4_device_registry.html (Class 11) and complete NM-FW01 and the other devices.
  • Check registry, fix every failed check.
  • Export CSV (Comma-Separated Values): LAB05_device_registry.csv.

Part 2: rules that enforce your zoning table, and their proof

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

12Put every machine in its zone13

  • Attach each VM's adapter to the VirtualBox network of its zone.
  • Give it a fixed address; the gateway and DNS (Domain Name System) server are the firewall of that zone.
  • Keep the LAB_03 host firewalls on.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

13Start the test services and the DNS name14

  • sudo python3 -m http.server 443 on NM-WEB01 and NM-INET01.
  • SMB (Server Message Block) share and SSH on NM-FS01.
  • Unbound override www.northmaple.lab → 192.168.20.10; internal networks only.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

14Generate your rule list and test plan15

  • Replace the ZONING rows of ex2_zoning_to_rules.py with your LAB_01 rows.
  • Run it: LAB05_rule_set.csv and LAB05_test_plan.csv.
  • Paste into the workbook: every rule must show yes.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

15Create the aliases16

  • Firewall ▸ Aliases: hosts, networks, PRIVATE, INTERNAL_NETS.
  • Add the port alias MGMT_PORTS = 22, 443 for Z5 and Z11.
  • Apply.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

16Publish the website17

  • Firewall ▸ NAT (Network Address Translation) ▸ Destination NAT: WAN, TCP (Transmission Control Protocol), WAN address, port 443 → NM_WEB01:443.
  • Description Z1 publish website, association None.
  • Save, Apply.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

17Create the rules in order18

  • Firewall ▸ Rules: choose the interface, add the rows of your CSV in order, with Log on every block and the zoning ID in each description.
  • Disable the default LAN rules only after Z5 works, then disable anti-lockout.
  • DMZ: Z12 above Z9. WAN: a per-source state limit on Z1.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

18Prove every rule19

  • Run the 17 tests from the machine each one names (Test-NetConnection, nc -zv -w 3, nslookup).
  • Screenshot the Live View log line of every block.
  • Type the observed result and evidence into the workbook; fix every FAIL.

Part 2, Class 12 (Saturday)

19Close properly and submit20

  • New encrypted backup, registry updated, snapshots named LAB05-done.
  • One ZIP: the Chapter 5 report (with notice box, copyright line, AI disclosure) plus the evidence folder.
  • Upload to the Omnivox Léa DropBox before Sunday, October 18, 2026, 11:59 pm EDT.

Footnotes: what may look different on your screen

  1. Every screen in the animations is a simplified recreation drawn for this course from the official documentation and release notes available on September 23, 2026. It is not a screenshot: colours, spacing and exact wording on your screen will differ.
  2. VirtualBox 7.2 (September 2026). The Manager window, the snapshot tools and the New VM wizard changed in 7.0 to 7.2 (7.1 and later ask for OS, Distribution and Version separately); a later 7.x or 8.0 release can move these buttons. Downloads: https://www.virtualbox.org/wiki/Downloads
  3. VBoxManage syntax as documented for VirtualBox 7.x. The output of natnetwork list can show extra lines (IPv6, loopback mappings) depending on the version. Manual: https://www.virtualbox.org/manual/
  4. The download page https://opnsense.org/download/ is redesigned from time to time. Installation images appear in January and July only: OPNsense 27.1, expected in January 2027, would change the file name and the checksum. Always take the checksum of your version from its release notes: https://docs.opnsense.org/releases/CE_26.7.html
  5. Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 format Get-FileHash slightly differently. On Windows 11, 7-Zip sits under Show more options in the right-click menu unless you enable its modern menu entry. 7-Zip: https://www.7-zip.org
  6. OPNsense installer menus as of 26.7 (text interface). Wording, option order and the proposed file system may change in a later release; the steps (keymap, UFS or ZFS, disk, root password, complete install) stay the same. Guide: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/install.html
  7. Console menu and questions as of 26.7; the question texts are shortened in the animation and may vary between versions.
  8. Each browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari) shows its own certificate warning page. The setup wizard pages are those of 26.7; a later version may reorder or rename them.
  9. OPNsense publishes a point release about every two weeks (26.7.4 on September 15, 2026). By the time you do the lab a newer 26.7.x may exist: install the newest one and record its number.
  10. Interface assignments moved to a new page in 26.7, and 26.7.3 started adding interface settings to that page: some fields may move between Assignments and the interface page in later 26.7.x versions.
  11. Administration and Users pages as of 26.7; option names (for example the SSH authentication settings) can change between versions.
  12. The registry page is the course file L4_device_registry.html from Class 11. The checks shown here are illustrative; your copy of the page is the reference.
  13. Linux connection names differ (Wired connection 1, enp0s3 …); Ubuntu Server uses netplan instead of nmcli; the Windows interface alias may be Ethernet 2. The VirtualBox network dialog depends on your VirtualBox version.
  14. Unbound DNS Overrides and Access Lists pages as of 26.7. Python's http.server module (Python 3) prints the same message on every current version.
  15. Output of the course script ex2_zoning_to_rules.py with the reference zoning table; your own rows give a different output.
  16. Aliases page as of 26.7 (the content display changed in 26.7.3). A rule accepts one port, one range or one alias, which is why Z5 and Z11 use the port alias MGMT_PORTS.
  17. The port forward page is called Destination NAT since 26.1; it was Port Forward before and is still Port Forward on pfSense CE. The list of filter-rule association options may differ.
  18. Since 26.7 the new rules page is the default (in 26.1 it was labelled Rules [new]; the old pages live in the optional os-firewall-legacy plugin), and the default LAN rules appear in this grid. The names of the advanced state-limit options vary, and 26.7.2 and 26.7.3 added options such as max-pkt-rate and received-on. Docs: https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/firewall.html
  19. Windows PowerShell and the netcat of your Linux distribution (OpenBSD nc, or Ncat https://nmap.org/ncat/) print slightly different messages. The Live View log was redesigned in 26.1; its columns may differ.
  20. Omnivox and Léa are run by each college: the DropBox page looks different from one college to another and can change at any time. Follow your college's instructions; the deadline stays Sunday, October 18, 2026, 11:59 pm EDT (Eastern Daylight Time).
  21. If you use pfSense CE (Community Edition) 2.9.0 instead of OPNsense, the installer (Netgate Installer, which needs Internet access), the first login (admin / pfsense) and the menus are different. Release notes: https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/releases/2-9-0.html
